solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nimble 24 about to be featured in this paper

indicators.note: something featured in a paper appears inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the clue appears in the Financial Times, abbreviated FT

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the fish from 24 is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 24-across, a fish

explanation.surface: A newspaper is about to run a story on a quick-moving fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this paper' is the Financial Times, where the puzzle appeared; 'about' reverses the fish from 24.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone fleet of foot is quick and nimble.

clue.text: Madness mostly in debt to fans

indicators.note: mostly means not the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: folly is foolishness or madness
owing money means being in debt

explanation.surface: It is mostly crazy to be indebted to your admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a following is a body of supporters or fans.

clue.text: Old strain in appendix

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
tension is strain

explanation.surface: An old injury, a strain, recorded in a document's appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appendix' tempts toward the body part; here it is an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an extension is an add-on to something, as an appendix is to a book.

clue.text: List out second bits of insider info

parts.note: to list is to lean over, to tip
off means out, as with a light

explanation.surface: List the second-rate pieces of inside knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a noun or 'make a list'; it is the verb meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tip-offs are private warnings or confidential hints from someone in the know.

clue.text: Dabbled in small stuff, extremely engrossed

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
stuff, as in material or substance, means matter

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word engrossed

explanation.surface: Someone who dabbled in trivia was nonetheless utterly absorbed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To smatter is an old verb meaning to have a superficial knowledge of, i.e. to dabble.

clue.text: Bond agent, the best senior officer left in eastern Prague

parts.note: super is short for superintendent, a senior police officer, and also means the best

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left within the letters taken from Prague
eastern means the right-hand, eastern end of the word Prague, its last half

explanation.surface: James Bond, the top agent, meets a senior officer left behind in eastern Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern' keeps the east end of PRAGUE, GUE, and 'in' places L within it. 'Bond' suggests 007, but the definition means an adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong adhesive is a bonding agent, so the clue's phrase describes it literally.

clue.text: Settle up in part of beer garden

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
part of the phrase beer garden contains the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Pay up for your share in a pub's beer garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle up' wants to be the definition, but 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to agree is to settle on something, come to terms.

clue.text: Containing a lot of drink, cask overturned — use this to wash

indicators.note: containing says the cask holds the next piece
overturned in a down clue means the letters run upwards

parts.note: a butt is a large cask

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A cask holding plenty of drink has been knocked over, so clean up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses the cask, giving TTUB. A twin tub is an old British washing machine with separate wash and spin drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is a washing machine, so the clue's phrase describes its purpose.

clue.text: Physicist about to introduce minute lozenge

indicators.note: introduce means bring inside, so the minute's letter goes within
about means turned round, so the physicist's name runs backwards

parts.note: Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist

explanation.surface: A scientist is about to bring in a tiny throat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives RHOB, and M goes in. 'minute' looks like tiny but is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric sense: a lozenge is a diamond shape, a rhombus.

clue.text: Novelist yelled oddly after party

indicators.note: after says the letters from yelled come after the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of yelled

explanation.surface: A writer was shouting strangely after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Arthur Conan Doyle or Roddy Doyle, both well-known novelists.

clue.text: Tight rim around half of cylinder

indicators.note: around says the rim encloses the next piece

parts.note: the lip of a vessel is its rim

indicators.note: half of keeps only the front two of the four letters

parts.note: a tube is a hollow cylinder

explanation.surface: A tight rim fits around half of a cylinder, like a seal or cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it describes the rim, but it is the definition, slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang idioms for being drunk: tight and lit up mean intoxicated.

clue.text: What might make minors pay up? Not this

definitions.text: What might make minors pay up? Not this

indicators.note: up, as in stirred up or mixed up, tells us to rearrange the letters before it

explanation.surface: Something that would make youngsters cough up money? Certainly not meanness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals the anagram of MINORS PAY; read whole, the clue also says stinginess is the last thing that would make anyone pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme meanness with money, the opposite of a willingness to hand cash over.

clue.text: Particular leaders of New World Order are overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so in an across clue the letters run backwards
leaders are the front letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Particular figures at the top of a New World Order are toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' gives NWO and 'are overthrown' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: your particular style is your individual, personal one.

clue.text: Nondescript story about poor Gavin's first otter

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the story is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a fable is a moral story

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged
first takes the opening letter of Gavin

explanation.surface: A dull tale about Gavin's sorry otter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges G plus the otter into ORGETT; 'about' has the story wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something nondescript is unremarkable and easily slips from memory.

clue.text: I strive to join the top in social climbers

parts.note: to vie is to compete or strive

indicators.note: the top in an across word is its first letter, here of social

explanation.surface: Someone claims to strive to reach the top of society, as social climbers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social climbers' looks like one phrase; 'social' only gives its first letter and 'climbers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ivy is a climbing plant, so these are plant climbers.

clue.text: Ex pilot flying new BrAitish glider hard

indicators.note: flying suggests things tossed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for British
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A former pilot flies a brand-new British glider with difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'BrAitish' is a typo for British in the source. 'glider' and 'pilot' share the flying scene, hiding that 'flying' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh was a famous American aviator, the first to fly solo nonstop across the Atlantic, now long dead.

clue.text: What remains of advantage following trap

indicators.note: following means the advantage comes after the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap
profit means gain or advantage

explanation.surface: What is left of a benefit after falling into a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is the amount left over once costs are taken off.

clue.text: An element of pity over my family getting upset about uni

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the pity sits above the rest

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity

indicators.note: about means going round the university letter
upset in a down clue means turned over, read upwards

parts.note: me and mine: mine means my family or people
U is short for university

explanation.surface: A sad story about my family turning against university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns MINE to ENIM, and 'about' wraps it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard metal of the platinum group, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Guy's old country is within range

indicators.note: is within says the old country sits inside the possessive

parts.note: a guy is a man, so his belongs to him
Malaya was the former name of the mainland part of Malaysia

explanation.surface: A man's former homeland lies within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Asian mountain chain containing Everest is a range.

clue.text: Maybe defer to mostly neglectful criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of neglectful is dropped

explanation.surface: Perhaps one should give way to a criminal who is largely careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NEGLECTFUL to NEGLECTFU, which 'criminal' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the knee is a show of deference; 'maybe' marks it as one example of deferring.

clue.text: Where brothers may scoff following false arrest

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Monks might jeer after being wrongly detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like mock; it means eat. A frater is a monastery refectory.
explanation.definitionFit: A frater is the dining hall of a monastery, where monks eat.

clue.text: Baseline return a little clumsy at heart

indicators.note: return means send back, so the small amount is read backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of clumsy

explanation.surface: Returning to a baseline, a slightly clumsy one at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TAD to DAT, and 'at heart' gives UM from the middle of CLUMSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a datum is a fixed reference level from which measurements are taken, a baseline.

clue.text: Blue mould left exposed, rotting

indicators.note: rotting suggests decay and breakdown, so the letters are rearranged
exposed means stripped of its covering, the outermost letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Decaying mould left uncovered is a depressing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips M and T off MOULD LEFT, and 'rotting' rearranges OULDLEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: feeling blue means sad, mournful.

clue.text: Mild caviare prepared for top brass

indicators.note: prepared, as food is made ready, signals the letters being reworked

explanation.surface: Mild caviar has been served to the senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a high-ranking naval officer is one of the senior commanders called top brass.

clue.text: Bring up unfinished ballot about major route

indicators.note: about means going round the road
unfinished drops the last letter

parts.note: a vote is a ballot
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Raise the matter of an incomplete vote over a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to bring up food is to vomit.

clue.text: Caught up with old man for a drink

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
up as written
pa is father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Caught up with father for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, a drink.

clue.text: Millions with open-ended agreements? I think not

indicators.note: open-ended means each of the agreements loses the letters at both its ends

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement, and the plural gives two lots of them

explanation.surface: Millions agreeing without conclusion? Hardly likely.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'agreements' stands for two AYES; 'open-ended' trims each to YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'my eye' is an exclamation of disbelief, meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Fish in regular spots in Easter Island

indicators.note: regular spots are letters taken at a fixed interval, here every fourth one starting with the first

explanation.surface: Fish caught at intervals around Easter Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 1, 5 and 9 of EASTER ISLAND give E, E, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eel is a long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Plan page about the French national symbol

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area

indicators.note: about means around, so page wraps the French article

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A plan of a page discussing France's national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the maple's foliage emblem is Canada's national symbol, on its flag.

clue.text: Not large, quite a small charming creature

indicators.note: not here means leave out the letter for large

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in fairly good
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Not big, but a fairly small and delightful little being.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fairy is a tiny magical being of folklore, often charming.

clue.text: Excited entrant is passing

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: An eager newcomer's enthusiasm is short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something transient is fleeting, only passing through.

clue.text: Punches male in bits below the belt?

indicators.note: in places the male abbreviation inside the next piece

parts.note: the lap is the part of the body below the waist when seated

explanation.surface: A boxer punches a man below the belt, a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below the belt' suggests a foul blow; here it just locates laps on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamp is British slang meaning to hit or punch someone.
